name: lsof
description: Lists open files — and on Linux, everything is a file: regular files, sockets, pipes, devices. The tool for "what is using this?"

flags.description: Which process holds this mount point busy.

examples.output:
COMMAND  PID   USER   FD  TYPE DEVICE SIZE NODE NAME
nginx   1024   root   6u  IPv4  18231      0t0  TCP *:http (LISTEN)
examples.explanation: Which process is bound to port 80 — the definitive answer to "address already in use".
Who has this file open — explains why you cannot delete or rotate it cleanly.
Finds processes keeping a mount busy — the missing piece before umount.
Every file, socket, and library one process currently holds open.

about: A deleted-but-open file keeps consuming space until its last user closes it — lsof | grep deleted finds these "ghost" files, the classic full-disk mystery. lsof needs root to see other users' files fully.
useCases: Track deleted files still holding disk space.
mistakes: Searching for a file by name without -p/+D and missing open-but-deleted entries.
